verifier_notes.method: Every one of the 131 records in R01.json was independently re-fetched on 2026-08-05. learning.sap.com and help.sap.com/saphelp_me150 static pages were re-fetched with WebFetch using exact-string presence prompts. All help.sap.com/docs SPA pages were re-rendered with the in-app browser (WebFetch returns only the title for those). Two pages (29/d4b6... and c5/72bb...) were re-checked a second time through the browser to rule out WebFetch rendering artefacts.
verifier_notes.tier_gate_applied: learning.sap.com treated as Tier 2 VENDOR-LEARNING: CONFIRMED accepted for product behaviour/UX/config-behaviour statements only. help.sap.com treated as Tier 1 OFFICIAL. No Tier 3 sources appear in this lane.
verifier_notes.systemic_finding: The lane's own gap #7 correctly identified that two product variants were mixed, but the individual records do not carry that scope. 18 records sourced from SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition (Enterprise Projects) documentation are written as general SAP PS statements. Each is marked OVERSTATED below with the correct scope named. A blueprint that treats these as classic on-premise SAP PS rules will encode constraints that classic PS does not impose.

results.what_source_actually_says: "The project definition is a framework for all the objects created within a project."
results.notes: Tier-2 product-behaviour statement; acceptable at this tier.

results.what_source_actually_says: "Before you create a WBS, you have to create a project definition." Confirmed verbatim on a second targeted exact-string pass.
results.notes: First re-fetch returned a paraphrase; a second exact-string pass confirmed the sentence is verbatim.

results.what_source_actually_says: "The project definition contains data that affects the entire project (for example, start and finish dates, organizational data, and planning parameters)."
results.notes: Confirmed verbatim on second exact-string pass.

results.what_source_actually_says: "It contains default values that can be passed on to the WBS elements."
results.notes: Source says values CAN be passed on, not that they always are. Corroborated more strongly by Tier-1 record R01-008.

results.what_source_actually_says: "The controlling area that you specify when you create a project definition is unique for the entire project."
results.notes: Independently corroborated by Tier-1 source of R01-006.

results.what_source_actually_says: "The project definition's controlling area is valid for the entire project and cannot be changed for a WBS element."
results.notes: Classic on-premise PS page (Organizational Data). Scope is correct as stated.

results.what_source_actually_says: "You can assign different plants, company codes, and business areas to WBS elements." The same page adds that profit center, object class, change number and currency are also assignable per WBS element, and that WBS currency is changeable only until currency-dependent data is saved.
results.notes: The currency-lock rule on the same page is a useful additional constraint the lane did not capture.

results.what_source_actually_says: "When you create new WBS elements or incorporate them into a WBS, the values from the project definition are copied into the WBS elements."
"The work breakdown structure (WBS) is a model of the project that organizes project tasks into a hierarchy."
"the functional basis for further planning steps in a project, for example, for process planning, cost planning, scheduling, capacity planning or costing"

"Structure element of the work breakdown structure (WBS). A WBS element describes either a certain task or a partial task that can be subdivided further." The page also notes (DIN 69 901) that a work package can be represented by either a WBS element or an activity.
results.notes: The DIN 69 901 note - a work package may be EITHER a WBS element OR an activity - is material to any WBS-to-Zoho mapping and was not captured in the lane.

results.what_source_actually_says: "You can divide these WBS elements at various levels until you reach the level of detail you require."
results.notes: Source says 'at various levels', which does NOT assert 'arbitrarily many levels' as the claim_text words it. No level ceiling is stated either way; the lane's gap note on this is correct.

results.what_source_actually_says: "Since the WBS is structured hierarchically, the data can be summarized and displayed at the corresponding higher-level WBS elements."
results.notes: Source says data CAN be summarized; the claim's 'values summarize upward' reads as automatic. Minor.

results.what_source_actually_says: "Evaluating aggregated data, Allocating budgets, Defining responsibilities"
"The work breakdown structure can be used to aggregate dates, costs, and commitments from the network activities."

results.replacement_quote: The WBS elements themselves would be used for planned and actual revenues, and they can also be used for budgeting, if required.
results.what_source_actually_says: The page states only what WBS elements ARE used for. It makes NO negative statement that revenue cannot be planned or posted on network activities. It also qualifies budgeting with 'if required', which the lane's quote silently dropped, along with the leading 'The'.
results.notes: HIGH IMPACT. The claim_text's exclusive clause 'not on network activities' is the researcher's inference, not the source's statement. A Zoho data model that hard-forbids revenue on activity-level objects would be resting on unsourced text. Narrower true statement: WBS elements are used for planned and actual revenues and may optionally be used for budgeting.

results.what_source_actually_says: "When you create a work breakdown structure, you must also enter a project profile for the project."

Full sentence: "The project profile contains default values and parameters for processing the project, for example, which settlement schema is valid, which factory calendar is used for time scheduling, or which settings are used for graphics."
results.notes: Claim's mention of factory calendar is supported by the full sentence, which the lane's quote truncated before.

results.what_source_actually_says: "If you create a work breakdown structure, the project profile is saved in the project definition." The page adds: "You can change default settings from the project profile when you are working with the work breakdown structure."
results.notes: The overridability sentence is important and was not captured: profile values are defaults, not locks.

results.what_source_actually_says: "There can only be one project profile per project." Preceded by: "In the project financial control process, you use project profiles to differentiate between accounting scenarios. The type of project profile influences a project's behavior with default information."
results.notes: Rendered via in-app browser. SCOPE CAVEAT: this is SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition. The four-way accounting typology on this page (Overhead / Investment / Statistical / Project with Revenue) is Cloud-specific. The one-profile-per-project half is independently corroborated for classic PS by the Tier-1 source of R01-019.

results.what_source_actually_says: "Coding masks serve as a display option for complex project numbers."
"The following characters are available for editing and structuring project numbers: X for alphanumeric characters, and 0 for numeric characters and special characters."
results.notes: The source sentence is itself ambiguously punctuated ('0 for numeric characters and special characters'); the claim's reading (X=alphanumeric, 0=numeric, plus separators) is the sensible one but the source does not cleanly separate the third category.

results.what_source_actually_says: "The way it is set up depends on the first characters of the project number. These characters serve as keys for coding projects."
results.notes: The second sentence, which the lane omitted, is what actually supports the 'coding key' half of the claim.

results.what_source_actually_says: Full sentence: "Even though you can make additions to the coding masks later, you cannot take anything away if WBSs have already been created using this project coding mask."
results.notes: The claim's trailing gloss 'numbering is effectively immutable' overshoots the source, which explicitly permits later ADDITIONS. Use 'append-only once projects exist', not 'immutable'.

results.what_source_actually_says: "you can maintain blocking checkboxes for standard structures (LkS) and operative structures (Lck). You cannot create new projects with this coding key if you maintain a blocking checkbox."
results.notes: Two separate blocking flags exist (standard vs operative structures); the claim collapses them into one.

results.what_source_actually_says: "The project coding mask defines how WBS element IDs are determined from the project ID."
results.notes: Rendered via in-app browser. SOURCING CAVEAT: the page renders under 'Production Engineering and Operations for Complex Assembly', Version 2025 FPS01 (Feb 2026), and opens 'Follow the steps here to define a project coding mask for complex assembly projects.' The quoted sentence is itself stated unconditionally, so the claim holds, but this is a product-specific how-to page, not the general PS coding-mask documentation.

results.what_source_actually_says: "The total length of a WBS ID, including project ID and all special characters, must not exceed 24 characters." The page also states you can assign up to 5 characters for the project coding ID.
results.notes: SOURCING CAVEAT (same page as R01-026): the ONLY source the lane offers for the 24-character cap is a Complex Assembly (PEO) how-to page. The sentence is unconditional so the verdict stands, but this is a load-bearing field-length constraint for the Zoho ID design and deserves a second, general PS citation before it is used as a hard design rule.

results.what_source_actually_says: "The WBS element with the shortest number is created in level 1."
Appears in the Prerequisites section: "In this coding mask you entered enough dashes to model all the levels in the project hierarchy."
results.notes: Source names dashes specifically; the claim generalises to 'separators'. Harmless but worth noting the mask separator in the example is a dash.

results.what_source_actually_says: "If you enter the special character in the WBS element field in your project, the system copies the number of the higher-level WBS elements into the field. If the new WBS element is the first one in the project hierarchy, the system copies the project definition." Worked example uses '@' and shows @-20 without a mask vs @20 with mask A-000-XXX-00-00, yielding A-123-LDZ-10-20.
results.notes: The root-element fallback (copies the project definition) and the separator-suppression-under-mask behaviour are both material to a Zoho ID-entry UX and were not captured in the lane.

results.what_source_actually_says: "You use operative indicators to define the characteristics of a WBS element and to specify what tasks the WBS element will perform during project execution."
results.notes: Tier 2 only, as the lane's gap #1 correctly flags.

results.what_source_actually_says: "WBS elements for which you want to plan costs are flagged as planning elements."
results.notes: Tier-2 product-behaviour statement, accepted at that tier. No Tier-1 corroboration exists in this lane for the planning-element indicator specifically.

results.what_source_actually_says: "WBS elements to which you want to post actual costs are flagged as account assignment elements."
results.notes: Partially corroborated at Tier 1 by the source of R01-040.

results.what_source_actually_says: "WBS elements where you want to plan or post revenues are flagged as billing elements."
results.notes: Corroborated at Tier 1 by the source of R01-035.

results.what_source_actually_says: "Billing Element is a project structure element against which a revenue can be planned and posted. It can either be a project or a WBS element."
results.notes: Rendered via in-app browser. S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition page, but the definition itself is generic and matches the Tier-2 classic-PS statement in R01-034, so no scope downgrade.

results.replacement_quote: However, a billing element cannot have another billing element in its subtree, nor can it be part of the subtree of another billing element.
results.what_source_actually_says: The quote matches verbatim, but it sits inside the 'Billing Element' page of SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition (Enterprise Projects), under 'Characteristics of a Billing Element'. The companion page (WBS Maintenance) files the same rule under a heading literally titled 'Special Rules for Projects with Revenue'.
results.notes: HIGHEST IMPACT SCOPE ERROR IN THE LANE. Narrower true statement: 'In SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition Enterprise Projects, in projects with revenue, billing elements cannot nest.' Classic on-premise SAP PS - the variant Atha Group is migrating FROM - imposes no such non-nesting constraint on the billing-element indicator. Encoding a non-nesting validation in the Zoho model on this basis would reject legitimate legacy SAP PS hierarchies at migration.

results.replacement_quote: All the WBS elements in the subtree of a billing element must have the same functional area and profit center as the billing element. When you create, include, or indent a WBS element below a billing element, these values are adjusted automatically.
results.what_source_actually_says: Quote matches verbatim but appears under the heading 'Special Rules for Projects with Revenue' on the S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition WBS Maintenance page. The rule is conditional on the project being a revenue project in that variant.
results.notes: Narrower true statement: applies to S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition Enterprise Projects, in projects with revenue, below a billing element. Note also the second sentence the lane omitted: the values are FORCE-ADJUSTED automatically, not merely validated - a materially different behaviour to implement.

results.replacement_quote: A project with revenue must contain at least one billing element.
results.what_source_actually_says: Quote matches verbatim. 'A project with revenue' is a named project-profile type in S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition (see the Project Profiles page), not a generic descriptor.
results.notes: Narrower true statement: in S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition, a project created with the 'Project with Revenue' profile must contain at least one billing element. The lane's claim_text reads as a universal accounting principle.

results.replacement_quote: You can maintain settlement rule for WBS elements. However, you will not be able to enter any settlement rule on the WBS elements in the billing element subtree.
results.what_source_actually_says: Quote matches, but the lane dropped the preceding sentence that establishes the general rule is the opposite: settlement rules CAN be maintained on WBS elements; the prohibition is the exception inside a billing-element subtree, in S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition.
results.notes: Narrower true statement as given in replacement_quote. Scope: S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition Enterprise Projects. Dropping the first sentence inverts the reader's default assumption about settlement rules.

results.what_source_actually_says: "To be able to assign a network to a WBS element, you must first identify the WBS element as an account assignment element."
results.notes: Classic on-premise PS. Correctly scoped.

results.what_source_actually_says: "The All Acct Asst Elem checkbox sets the account assignment checkbox for all WBS elements."
"Using the Only One Root checkbox, you define that there can only be one top WBS element."
results.notes: Implies multi-root WBS is possible by default in classic PS - a structural fact worth carrying into the Zoho model.

results.what_source_actually_says: "The Statistical checkbox determines whether costs can be debited from a WBS element or whether statistical costs can only be posted for it."
results.notes: Tier-2 behaviour statement; corroborated at Tier 1 by the source of R01-046.

results.replacement_quote: A statistical project is used for planning and monitoring purposes. When you set the statistical flag for a project, this flag applies to the WBS elements present in the project hierarchy. Upon saving the project for the first time, you cannot change the selection of this flag.
results.what_source_actually_says: Quote matches, but it describes the 'Statistical Project' PROJECT PROFILE TYPE in SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition. The page adds a hard irreversibility rule the lane omitted entirely: after first save the flag cannot be changed. It also requires a default cost center at WBS level.
results.notes: Narrower true statement: scope is S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition statistical projects. The omitted irreversibility-after-first-save rule and the mandatory default cost center are both design-relevant and should be added.

results.replacement_quote: Statistical WBS elements cannot be settled or carry overheads.
results.what_source_actually_says: Quote matches verbatim on the S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition Project Profiles page.
results.notes: Narrower true statement: scope is S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition. The 'cannot be settled' half IS independently corroborated for classic PS by the source of R01-046 (which states the statistical designation prevents settlement); the 'cannot carry overheads' half has Cloud-only support in this lane.

results.what_source_actually_says: Full sentence: "You define the order or WBS element as 'statistical' by setting an indicator in the model order or the project profile (or directly in the master record of the order or WBS element)." The page also states the statistical designation prevents settlement and limits use to planning and budget monitoring.
results.notes: The lane's quote truncated before the parenthetical that supports the claim's third route ('directly on the master record'); the full sentence does support it.

results.what_source_actually_says: "The Project Type can be used as a selection criterion in the Information System."
"The Level of Detail field specifies the number of hierarchy levels that the system displays when a project is opened in a particular processing transaction."
results.notes: First re-fetch returned a truncated form; second targeted exact-string pass confirmed the full sentence including 'when a project is opened in a particular processing transaction'.

results.what_source_actually_says: "The Display Options field determines whether WBS elements are mainly displayed according to key, short ID, or description in tabular overviews."
results.notes: Absent from the first re-fetch extract; confirmed present verbatim on a second targeted exact-string pass.

results.what_source_actually_says: "A network can represent the sequence of activities in a project or the sequence of a single activity within a project."
results.notes: Verified twice: WebFetch and in-app browser.

results.what_source_actually_says: "During the life of a project, networks are used as a basis for planning, analyzing, controlling and monitoring schedules, dates, and resources.(such as personnel, machines, PRTs, materials, documents, and drawings)."
results.notes: The lane's quote drops the leading 'During the life of a project,' but is otherwise an exact substring.

results.replacement_quote: In the Project System networks are activity-on-mode networks.
results.what_source_actually_says: The page reads 'activity-on-MODE networks', not 'activity-on-node'. Verified twice independently: once via WebFetch and once by rendering the page in the in-app browser, which returned the same word. The page nowhere mentions 'activity-on-arrow' and draws no contrast with any alternative network notation.
results.notes: TWO PROBLEMS. (1) The evidence_quote is not verbatim - the researcher silently corrected what is almost certainly a typo in the SAP source without flagging it, which breaks quote traceability. (2) The claim's second half, 'not activity-on-arrow', has no basis in the source at all; it is an inference. The substantive point may well be true, but this lane does not evidence it. Re-source from a page that names the precedence-diagramming method explicitly before relying on it.

results.what_source_actually_says: "Assignments to other objects, for example, project definition, WBS element or sales document" - appears in the Network Headers section.
Full sentence: "In header-assigned networks the values in the Costing section of the supplementary data screen of the network header are not default values, but are binding for the whole network."
results.notes: The lane's quote stops before 'but are binding for the whole network' - the clause that actually carries the claim. Full sentence supports it.

results.what_source_actually_says: "you can copy the dates from the project definition into the basic dates of the network."
"the project definition will be copied automatically when the assignment is made."

The page attributes the five characteristics to German standard DIN 69 900: "They have a duration. They have a defined start and a defined finish. They are processed without interruption. Resources are needed to execute them. They incur costs."
results.notes: The lane's evidence_quote covers only one of the five characteristics the claim asserts; the other four are on the same page, so the claim holds. Worth recording that this is a DIN 69 900 definition SAP adopts, not an SAP-invented rule.

results.what_source_actually_says: "Resources are needed to execute them."
"you determine the amount of Work produced by machines or persons, and use this information in resource planning to plan the capacity requirement."
"Using external processing you determine which services are required from other companies to carry out the project."
results.notes: The source sentence does not itself say 'run through purchasing'; that part of the claim_text is not carried by the quoted sentence.

results.what_source_actually_says: "Using External Services Management you plan unplanned and planned services for carrying out the project."
results.notes: As with R01-060, 'procured through purchasing' is not in the quoted sentence.

results.what_source_actually_says: "you plan primary costs, for example, travel costs."
"Relationships determine the chronological sequence of activities in a network or a standard network."
"These dependencies are represented by relationships in which one activity is the predecessor or the successor of another activity."
"The type of the relationship determines how the individual activities are linked with each other."
"This is the relationship between the end of an activity to the beginning of the following activity." All four types (FS, SS, FF, SF) are enumerated on the page.
"SF relationships are seldom used in practice. You can usually change SF relationships to FS relationships by changing the sequence of the activities."
results.notes: Second sentence, omitted from the lane's quote, is what supports the claim's 'usually rewritten as Finish-Start' half. Supports a scope decision to omit SF from the Zoho model.

results.what_source_actually_says: "A subnetwork is a network which covers only part of a project and is linked in relationships with other subnetworks in the same project."
"The network profile for the superior network is not copied into the subnetwork." Appears in a Note within the Structure section.
results.notes: Notable as an explicit EXCEPTION to the general downward-inheritance pattern the lane establishes elsewhere.

results.what_source_actually_says: "In Customizing for the Project System you can define the network type and the network parameters."
results.notes: The source says where they ARE defined; it does not explicitly say 'not per project' as the claim_text asserts. Weak inference, but consistent with Customizing semantics.

results.what_source_actually_says: "In general milestones are used to mark the transition between various phases or departments."
"You can create milestones in networks, standard networks, work breakdown structures (WBS) and standard work breakdown structures (standard WBS)."
"You cannot create milestones for activity elements."
results.notes: Note the distinction between an ACTIVITY (milestones allowed) and an ACTIVITY ELEMENT (not allowed).

results.what_source_actually_says: "When the milestone is reached, the actual date of the milestone is copied into the billing plan."
"Predefined milestone functions are used in networks to trigger a sequence of events for a particular business process."

Full sentence: "If you enter both a system status and a user status for a milestone function, the system triggers the function both when the system status changes and when the user status changes." The page also notes manual triggering is possible during activity confirmation.
results.notes: The lane's quote omits the conditional 'If you enter both...' but the claim_text correctly reconstructs it.

results.what_source_actually_says: "Milestones assigned to network activities enable the triggering of milestone functions, such as creating a new network, releasing follow-up activities, or starting a workflow task."
results.notes: Corroborated at Tier 1 by the Milestone Functions page (source of R01-075), which lists the same functions.

results.what_source_actually_says: "Milestone trend analysis is a simple method for analyzing the dates in a project and comparing them with planned data." The page adds: "The scheduled dates of the milestones, which are relevant for the course of the project, are compared at various points in time."
results.notes: The second sentence is what actually supports the claim's 'captured on different report dates' element.

results.what_source_actually_says: "If the project runs according to plan, the curve remains horizontal."

"In the Project System there are several different standard structures that you can use as templates to create operative structures." The page then enumerates four: standard networks, standard project definitions, standard work breakdown structures, and standard milestones.
results.notes: The enumeration of exactly four standard structure types is on this page and directly contradicts R01-129 - see that record.

results.what_source_actually_says: Full sentence: "A further advantage of standardizing project structures is that it makes the processing of projects more transparent, enables the comparison of projects and subsequently facilitates project controlling."
"Neutral work breakdown structure that can be used more than once and serves as a template for creating operative work breakdown structures."
"You can link standard networks with standard work breakdown structures and so create templates not only for the organization of a project but also for its processing."
"When you use a standard network that is assigned to a standard WBS to create an operative network an operative WBS is also created."
"However if you create an operative WBS from a standard WBS to which a standard network is assigned, an operative network is not created."
results.notes: Genuine asymmetry, correctly captured. Directly relevant to any Zoho template-instantiation design.

results.what_source_actually_says: "Neutral project definition, which can be used to create operative project definitions or standard project definitions as templates."
"Project-neutral network structure, which can be used as a template when creating other standard networks or operative networks."
Full passage: "It is not possible to plan operative data with standard work breakdown structures. For example, you cannot use a standard WBS for cost planning or time scheduling purposes."
results.notes: The preceding sentence is the general rule; the lane quoted only the example.

results.what_source_actually_says: "You also cannot maintain settlement rules in standard WBS elements."
results.notes: Tier-2 product-behaviour statement, accepted at that tier.

results.what_source_actually_says: "In the standard work breakdown structure, only the definition has a status."
"The status of the definition is Created (standard WBS) (CRES), Released (standard WBS) (RELS) or Closed (standard WBS) (CLOS)."
results.notes: Note the source phrases these as alternatives ('is X or Y or Z'), which supports the claim's 'three statuses' reading.

results.what_source_actually_says: "You can use an existing WBS, a section of the project hierarchy, or a standard WBS as a template."
"With root: The selected WBS element is included. Without root: Only the subordinate WBS elements are included." Appears in the table describing copy options.
results.notes: Classic on-premise PS. Note this differs from the S/4HANA Cloud include behaviour cited in R01-095, where inclusion is always with subtree and no with/without-root choice is offered.

results.what_source_actually_says: "If the WBS element to be included has additional WBS elements subordinate to it, the system automatically copies these lower-level hierarchy elements."

results.replacement_quote: Note, however, that a WBS element is always copied, included, shifted, or deleted with all the WBS elements in its subtree.
results.what_source_actually_says: Quote matches verbatim, but the page is 'Work Breakdown Structure Maintenance' for SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition, Version 2608, and the sentence is explicitly about operations 'in the Project Planning app'.
results.notes: Narrower true statement: in the S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition Project Planning app, copy/include/shift/delete always act on the whole subtree. This is NOT stated of classic on-premise PS, where R01-093 documents an explicit with-root / without-root choice on include. The two records are in tension precisely because they describe different products.

results.replacement_quote: By choosing (Indent), you shift the selected WBS element down one structure level to the subtree of the preceding WBS element.
results.what_source_actually_says: Quote matches. The page also adds a status side-effect the lane omitted: if a Created WBS element is indented below a Released one, the system auto-releases it and its whole subtree on next save.
results.notes: Narrower true statement: scope is the S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition Project Planning app. The omitted auto-release-on-indent side-effect is design-relevant.

results.replacement_quote: By choosing (Outdent), you shift the selected WBS element up one structure level to the position next to its previous parent. WBS elements succeeding the selected WBS element on its original structure level are added to the subtree of the outdented WBS element.
results.what_source_actually_says: Quote matches, but the lane's claim_text stops one sentence too early and therefore misses outdent's second, non-obvious effect: succeeding siblings are ABSORBED INTO the outdented element's subtree.
results.notes: Two defects: (1) scope is S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition Project Planning app; (2) the claim describes outdent as a simple one-level promotion, which is materially incomplete. An implementer building this from the lane record would produce the wrong behaviour.

results.replacement_quote: By choosing (Move Up) or (Move Down), you can rearrange the sequence of the WBS elements within one structure level. However, this only applies to WBS elements that have the same parent node. You cannot move a WBS element to a new parent.
results.what_source_actually_says: Quote matches. 'You cannot move a WBS element to a new parent' is scoped to the Move Up / Move Down functions specifically - the same page's drag-and-drop section explicitly DOES allow moving an element across structure levels.
results.notes: Scope: S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition Project Planning app. The claim_text does correctly limit itself to move up/down, but the bare quote is dangerous if lifted out of context, since it reads as a global 'no reparenting' rule that the same page contradicts two sections later.

results.replacement_quote: Drop a WBS element between two WBS elements to insert it at the structure level of these WBS elements. Drop a WBS element on another WBS element to insert it at the structure level below this WBS element.
results.what_source_actually_says: Both halves of the claim are present verbatim; the lane quoted only the second. Same auto-release-on-drop side-effect applies as with indent.
results.notes: Narrower true statement: scope is the S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition Project Planning app drag-and-drop, not SAP PS generally. Classic PS Project Builder is not documented here as having this behaviour.

results.replacement_quote: The system generates the WBS element ID based on the ID of the parent element and uses the same value for the WBS element name. It derives the following values from the project header: the organizational assignments of the WBS element, its Public Sector Management attributes and joint venture accounting attributes, its calendar, and control parameters, such as costing sheet, investment profile, or the default cost center for statistical postings.
results.what_source_actually_says: Quote matches. Scope is S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition. Note the ID is derived from the PARENT ELEMENT, whereas the classic-PS mechanism documented in R01-026 derives WBS IDs from the PROJECT ID via the coding mask - two different derivation mechanisms in two different products.
results.notes: Narrower true statement: scope is S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition. This record and R01-026 describe competing ID-derivation models; the blueprint must pick one and say which SAP variant it is emulating. The second sentence also gives a much fuller inheritance list than R01-008 and should be captured.

results.replacement_quote: You cannot delete WBS elements if you have already planned costs. In projects with revenue, you cannot delete a WBS element if you have already planned revenue, maintained a settlement rule, or assigned a sales order item to it.
results.what_source_actually_says: Quote matches. The page also imposes a status precondition the lane omitted: to delete, the WBS element and its entire subtree must have processing status Created.
results.notes: Narrower true statement: scope is S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition. Three additional deletion blockers (planned revenue, settlement rule, sales order item) and the Created-status precondition were all omitted; the lane's single-condition version understates the constraint substantially.

results.what_source_actually_says: "The active system status determines which business transactions you can perform with work breakdown structures and WBS elements."
results.notes: Classic on-premise PS SYSTEM status. Distinct from the Cloud PROCESSING status of R01-104..106.

results.what_source_actually_says: "WBS elements that are completed from a technical point of view, but where you still expect costs to accrue." Appears under the 'Technically completed (TECO)' heading.
results.notes: Correctly scoped to classic PS. Note the S/4HANA Cloud equivalent is named 'Completed', not 'Technically Completed' - do not merge the two vocabularies in the blueprint.

results.replacement_quote: The processing status of a project or WBS element influences the status of the lower-level WBS elements and vice versa.
results.what_source_actually_says: Quote matches verbatim on the page 'Processing Status for Projects and WBS Elements' (SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition). The same page explicitly distinguishes PROCESSING status from SYSTEM status: 'Projects and WBS elements also have a system status which is related to their processing status but documents their current processing stage in a more detailed way.'
results.notes: Two defects: (1) scope is S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition Enterprise Projects; (2) the claim_text says 'Status propagates', flattening the source's own explicit distinction between processing status and system status. R01-102 covers classic PS system status - a different mechanism. Naming both simply 'status' in the blueprint would merge two distinct SAP concepts.

results.replacement_quote: All the lower-level WBS elements that have the status Created are automatically released along with it.
results.what_source_actually_says: Quote matches. The page shows the same cascade pattern applies at Completed (Released children auto-Complete) and Closed (Completed children auto-Close), which the lane did not capture.
results.notes: Narrower true statement: scope is S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition processing status. The cascade is a general pattern across three transitions, not only release - capturing only one of three understates the model.

results.replacement_quote: This status cannot be set manually. It is set automatically when any of the lower-level WBS elements are set to Released.
results.what_source_actually_says: Quote matches verbatim, under the 'Partially Released' processing status value.
results.notes: Narrower true statement: scope is S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition processing status. Classic on-premise PS has its own PREL system status whose semantics are not evidenced anywhere in this lane.

results.what_source_actually_says: Full sentence: "A project version is created for operative structures or in the information system and captures the state of a project at a certain point in time or with a certain status."
results.notes: The lane's quote truncated before the clause that carries the claim; the full sentence supports it.

results.what_source_actually_says: "A plan version is created in accounting and stores different cost plans for a project, such as an 'optimistic' and a 'pessimistic' plan."
Full sentence: "A selection version is used only in the information system for processing in the background and saves project data matching certain selection criteria for retrieval."
results.notes: The lane's quote stops before the clause supporting 'snapshots of data matching selection criteria'; the full sentence supports the claim.

results.what_source_actually_says: "When you create project versions in the information system, you can choose whether you want all of the current data or a subset of data."
results.notes: Scoped to versions created IN THE INFORMATION SYSTEM, which the claim_text does not say.

results.what_source_actually_says: "The MTA-relevant indicator in this window stipulates that the data from this version can be used in milestone trend analysis."
"Project versions are not created in real time. This means, that under certain circumstances, there is a time lag between..."
results.notes: Source says 'not in real time' with a time-lag consequence; the claim's word 'asynchronously' is a reasonable gloss but is not the source's word.

results.what_source_actually_says: "The structure overview is displayed. The different project versions are displayed in different colors."
"The Version Profile determines whether status-dependent project versions are written and with which data."
"it is often necessary to simulate and save changes to a project, without affecting the operative project." Appears in the Purpose section.
"There are no system statuses in simulation versions." Appears in the Constraints section.
results.notes: Appearing under Constraints is itself significant - this is a documented limitation, not a design feature.

results.what_source_actually_says: "The Simulation Profile determines which texts are copied to and from simulation versions."
"You can create, change or display all project structure data in one transaction." Appears in the Features section.
"All the editing transactions for work breakdown structures and networks can be executed in the Project Builder." Appears in the Integration section.
"You can define a user-specific worklist and a user-specific templates pool."
"The hierarchy of your current project is displayed in a separate screen area."
results.notes: The source says 'separate screen area'; the claim adds 'persistent' and 'beside the detail work area', neither of which is in the quoted sentence.

results.what_source_actually_says: "The structure contains the selected project data of the current project, along with its hierarchical relationships."
results.notes: Source says 'the SELECTED project data', which the claim renders as 'current project data' - slightly broader.

results.what_source_actually_says: "You can use the Project Builder to maintain any object in the SAP PS, except for the assignment of Production Resources/Tools (PRT)."

Quote matches. The full inventory on the page is: Basic Data, Dates, Assignments, Responsibilities, Control Data, Total, Milestones, Documents, PS Texts, User fields, Administration, Progress, Superior elements, Settlement Rules, Long text, Investment Program, Summarization. The page also notes detail screens are customizable in Project System Customizing.
results.notes: The lane's evidence_quote is a pure pointer sentence that names none of the tabs the claim_text asserts. The tab list IS on the page, so the claim holds, but the quote is non-probative on its own. Capture the full 17-item list - it is the closest thing this lane has to a WBS field inventory.

results.replacement_quote: By assigning an investment profile to the project or WBS element and upon releasing the WBS element, the asset under construction is generated. All or parts of the costs must be settled to the asset under construction.
results.what_source_actually_says: Quote matches, on the 'Investment Project' section of the S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition Project Profiles page. The page also states the investment profile is NOT a mandatory field, and that once the WBS element is technically complete all subsequent postings - including earlier post-release postings - settle to the fixed asset.
results.notes: Narrower true statement: scope is S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition investment projects. The omitted 'investment profile is not mandatory' qualifier and the technically-complete settlement-redirection rule are both material to a CAPEX/AuC design, which is the core of this engagement.

results.replacement_quote: Depending on the type of project and the emphasis in project monitoring, you structure your project in the Project System using the operative structures work breakdown structure (WBS) and/or networks Standard structures, for example standard WBS and standard networks allow you standardize and reuse structures and sequences of events in your projects.

contradictions.lane_asserted: NEGATIVE / UNEVIDENCED: the dedicated Standard Milestone definition page could not be retrieved (fetch_status recorded as 404); standard milestones are only referenced indirectly.
contradictions.source_actually_says: The page at help.sap.com/saphelp_me150/helpdata/EN/c5/72bb53707db44ce10000000a174cb4/content.htm returns HTTP 200 with full content, titled 'Standard Milestones'. It states: 'Standard milestones are used exclusively in the Project System as a source for creating milestones and other standard milestones.' It further documents milestone groups ('You can combine different standard milestones in a milestone group. For example, you can group together all milestones that are relevant for earned value analysis.') and the copy path into activities and WBS elements.
contradictions.verification_method: Re-fetched with WebFetch AND independently re-rendered in the in-app browser on 2026-08-05. Both returned full content.
contradictions.corroborating_evidence: The Standard Structures page (9c/72bb53707db44ce10000000a174cb4), already cited by the lane for R01-080 and R01-081, explicitly lists 'Standard milestones for creating milestones in networks' as one of the four standard structure types - so the lane already held Tier-1 evidence that this object exists and is documented.
contradictions.impact: A real Tier-1 source was wrongly written off as unavailable. The lane therefore has no records on standard milestones or milestone groups, and gaps entry #2 in R01.json is false and must be removed. Milestone groups tied to earned value analysis are directly relevant to progress-measurement design.

contradictions.lane_asserted: evidence_quote: 'In the Project System networks are activity-on-node networks.' claim_text: 'SAP PS networks are activity-on-node graphs, not activity-on-arrow.'
contradictions.source_actually_says: The page reads 'In the Project System networks are activity-on-mode networks.' - the word is 'mode', not 'node'. The page nowhere mentions 'activity-on-arrow' and draws no contrast with any alternative notation.
contradictions.verification_method: Confirmed twice independently on 2026-08-05: WebFetch flagged the discrepancy unprompted, and a follow-up in-app browser render of the same URL returned the identical wording.
contradictions.corroborating_evidence: None in-lane. No other cited page in R01 discusses network notation.
contradictions.impact: Not a substantive error - almost certainly a long-standing typo in the SAP source - but the researcher silently corrected the source text without flagging it, which breaks quote traceability, and then appended an 'not activity-on-arrow' contrast that the source does not make. Both halves need re-sourcing before use.

summary.variant_mixing_verdict: CONFIRMED AS A REAL AND UNMITIGATED PROBLEM. The lane's own gap #7 anticipated it, but 18 records drawn from SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition (Enterprise Projects) documentation are written as general SAP PS statements with no variant named in claim_text: R01-036, 037, 038, 039, 044, 045, 095, 096, 097, 098, 099, 100, 101, 104, 105, 106, 125, plus R01-016 for a different reason. Two concrete collisions are already visible inside the lane: (a) R01-093 (classic PS offers a with-root / without-root choice on include) versus R01-095 (Cloud always includes the whole subtree); (b) R01-026 (WBS IDs derived from the PROJECT ID via coding mask) versus R01-100 (WBS IDs derived from the PARENT ELEMENT ID). These are not compatible descriptions of one system. Every downstream section that consumes these records must name the SAP variant it is emulating.
